'''Václav Edvard "Vic" Beneš''' (born July 24, 1930) is a [[Czech-American]] [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to the theory of [[stochastic processes]], [[queueing theory]] and [[control theory]], as well as the design of telecommunications [[switch]]es.

He studied under [[John George Kemeny|John Kemeny]] and gained a doctorate in [[mathematics]] at [[Princeton University]] (1953) on a treatise on ''[[Mathematical logic]]''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=29862}}</ref>

He then worked for [[Bell Labs]] until 1986,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cm.bell-labs.com/cm/ms/center/frmdir.html |title=Former members of the Math Center |access-date=2002-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020214221501/http://cm.bell-labs.com/cm/ms/center/frmdir.html |archive-date=2002-02-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  contributing to [[Kalman filter]] theory<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://140.78.137.200/ifac50/Project_G/Control-Theory-Timeline.htm |title=Control theory timeline |access-date=2007-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070813090531/http://140.78.137.200/ifac50/Project_G/Control-Theory-Timeline.htm |archive-date=2007-08-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as well as the [[Clos network#Beneš network|Beneš network]], a [[permutation network]] of the [[Clos network]] type.  In the 1980s he held a position at [[Columbia University]] as well. He has continued to publish independently since 1989.

He was elected [[IEEE Fellow]] (1991) for "contributions to the structure of telephone connecting networks, [[stochastic control]], and [[nonlinear filtering]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ieee.org/web/membership/fellows/Chronology/1990.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071214052819/http://www.ieee.org/web/membership/fellows/Chronology/1990.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 December 2007|title=IEEE Fellow Class of 1990|website=[[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) |accessdate=5 March 2024}}</ref>
The ''Benesfest'' was celebrated at [[Columbia University]] (2001) to honor his 70th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cap.columbia.edu/|title=CAP|website=cap.columbia.edu|accessdate=5 March 2024}}</ref>  He resides in [[Millburn, New Jersey]] (since 1985) where he has been a long-time [[mountain climber]]<ref>[http://www.research.att.com/~njas/doc/interview.html Interview] with [[Neil Sloane]]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.adirondackmountainguides.com/testimonials.html |title=Testimonial |access-date=2007-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070807191521/http://www.adirondackmountainguides.com/testimonials.html |archive-date=2007-08-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and member of the [[American Alpine Club]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nysalpineclub.org/ |title=New York Section of the Alpine Club |access-date=9 August 2007 |archive-date=19 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070819165347/http://nysalpineclub.org/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> and currently heads the local historical society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mshhistsoc.org/|title=Home|website=Millburn-Short Hills Historical Society|accessdate=5 March 2024}}</ref>

He is a relative of the former President of Czechoslovakia [[Edvard Beneš]] and politician [[Vojta Beneš]]. [[Emilie Benes Brzezinski]], a sculptor, was his sister.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PxBbAAAAYAAJ&pg=RA3-PA46 |title=Princeton Alumni Weekly |date=1949 |publisher=Princeton University Press |language=en}}</ref>

His first wife Janet was the daughter of [[Philip Franklin]] and niece of [[Norbert Wiener]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Franklin.html|title = Philip Franklin - Biography}}</ref>

==Books==
*''General stochastic processes in the theory of queues'' ([[Addison-Wesley]], 1963)
*''Mathematical Theory of Connecting Networks and Telephone Traffic'' ([[Academic Press]], 1965)

*''Nonexistence of strong nonanticipating solutions to stochastic DEs: implications for functional DEs, filtering, and control.'' [[Stochastic Processes Applied]] 5:3, 243–263., 1977
